title: Event-triggered Implicit Perturbation for Zeroth-Order Fine-Tuning of Spiking Transformers
summary: Replaces explicit read-modify-write weight perturbation with perturbation sums from dedicated hardware attached to an IMC array for zeroth-order fine-tuning of spiking networks. Compared with the simplified variant, it requires 40%-46% more silicon area and 15%-49% more energy per operation, plus custom 16 nm CMOS fabrication or synthesis. It is a circuit for SNNs, rather than software deployable on a 24 GB GPU or through a third-party API.
rationale: Circuit design for IMC spiking-network accelerators, without a conventional language-model or GPU software component the reader can adopt.
technique: Implicit zeroth-order perturbation for IMC spiking networks

claims.statement: Replaces explicit read-modify-write weight perturbation with perturbation sums from dedicated hardware attached to an IMC array for zeroth-order fine-tuning of spiking networks. Compared with the simplified variant, it requires 40%-46% more silicon area and 15%-49% more energy per operation, plus custom 16 nm CMOS fabrication or synthesis. It is a circuit for SNNs, rather than software deployable on a 24 GB GPU or through a third-party API.
IPZO reduces perturbation energy to 0.46x-0.83x of explicit weight perturbation; PGU-XOR matches software RNG accuracy, 76.41% versus 76.53% on CIFAR-10, while PGU-Reuse loses 9.56 points.

exposure_map.finding: On CIFAR-10, PGU-XOR reaches 76.41% accuracy, versus 66.85% for PGU-Reuse and 76.53% for the software Randint reference.
exposure_map.interpretation: The gain is strongest against the reuse baseline. The software reference remains slightly ahead.
exposure_map.limitation: These are the authors’ spiking-model results. They do not establish quality gains for GLM or Kimi.
exposure_map.next_check: Repeat the same task and perturbation baselines with fixed seeds before testing another architecture.

exposure_map.finding: The hardware study uses a 128 × 16 in-memory array and a custom perturbation generator in 16-nm CMOS, evaluated after chip layout.
exposure_map.interpretation: The reported savings concern perturbation energy. They cannot price a complete training run or an A100/H200 rental.
exposure_map.limitation: GPU memory needs, total system energy, and rental cost remain unknown.
exposure_map.next_check: First establish a runnable implementation and measure its full memory footprint and wall-clock cost.
exposure_map.source_excerpt: All hardware results reported in this section are obtained from post-layout implementations

exposure_map.finding: At 1 GHz, perturbation throughput falls from 4.10 to 0.51 TOPS as accumulation grows from one to eight cycles.
exposure_map.interpretation: Smaller circuitry trades throughput for area. The paper’s no-penalty condition requires the generator to keep pace with the in-memory array.
exposure_map.limitation: This is circuit throughput. Startup time, time to first token, and slow-request latency are not established.
exposure_map.next_check: Measure startup, median and p95 request latency separately on a complete implementation.
exposure_map.source_excerpt: lowering the throughput from 4.10 TOPS at c = 1 to 2.05, 1.02 and 0.51 TOPS

exposure_map.limitation: The reviewed architecture and experiments do not establish a deployment, monitoring, or rollback procedure.
exposure_map.next_check: Define checkpoint recovery, failure detection, and rollback behavior before a service trial.

exposure_map.finding: Applying this method requires the spiking model, in-memory compute path, and perturbation generator to work together.
exposure_map.limitation: A drop-in implementation for GLM-4.7-Flash, Kimi, or a conventional GPU inference server has not been established.
exposure_map.next_check: Locate runnable code and verify the architecture mapping before renting GPUs for this technique.
exposure_map.source_excerpt: the IMC array executes the standard MVM with the input spike vector

exposure_map.limitation: The reviewed source does not establish data-access controls, isolation, or resistance to malicious inputs.
exposure_map.next_check: Review input handling, model access, and isolation for the actual implementation before using private data.

exposure_map.finding: Spikingformer starts from ImageNet-1K pretraining; 75% of its parameters stay frozen during CIFAR-10 fine-tuning. SpikeGPT is fully fine-tuned on WikiText.
exposure_map.interpretation: This requires model adaptation and training data. It is not an inference-server setting.
exposure_map.limitation: Pretraining and data preparation are outside the quoted perturbation-energy comparison.
exposure_map.next_check: Account for checkpoints, dataset preparation, training, and evaluation in the experiment budget.
exposure_map.source_excerpt: CIFAR-10 with 75% of its parameters frozen, leaving 16.6M trainable parameters

exposure_map.limitation: The paper describes its circuit settings and benchmarks. Released hardware design files, exact seeds, and runnable evaluation scripts have not been verified.
exposure_map.next_check: Locate and pin the code, checkpoints, datasets, and hardware design; then attempt the smallest reported experiment.

equations.headline: Perturb the output, keep the weights in place
equations.explanation: Distributivity separates the weighted input from its perturbation contribution. Their sum reconstructs the perturbed output.
equations.objective: Avoid rewriting stored weights during perturbation evaluations.
equations.evidence: Section IV-A establishes algebraic equivalence. This identity alone does not establish an energy saving.

equations.headline: Find the energy break-even point
equations.explanation: R compares implicit and explicit perturbation energy. The numerator grows with batch size B and time steps T; R below one favors IPZO.
equations.objective: Identify workloads where avoided memory operations outweigh perturbation generation.
equations.evidence: At B = 64 and T = 4, the authors report ratios of 0.83 in BIT8 and 0.46 in BIT1. Figure 15 compares post-layout IPZO simulation with estimated EPZO energy. This is perturbation energy in a 16-nm IMC design, not measured GPU inference cost.
